title: Reefer Cargo Services: Temperature Excursions and Excursion Credits
content:
The recorder in every Reefer Cargo Services unit logs the return-air temperature, and the line keeps a record of each period in which it strays from the instructed set point. This page defines what counts as an excursion, when an excursion earns the service a credit, and how large that credit is.

## Clause

An excursion is a period during which the return-air temperature remains outside the band formed by the set point plus or minus the tier's tolerance. Its length is measured in whole logging intervals of the unit's recorder. The recorder logs every excursion, and the line enters each one on the service's record, with a nil amount, whatever caused it.

A service earns an excursion credit when an excursion has lasted at least the tier's qualifying number of minutes, provided that qualifying number is above zero, and when the excursion was not caused by the shipper's own instruction, by a set point unsuited to the needs of the commodity, or by cargo loaded warmer than the set point. The credit is the tier's credit percentage of the credit basis, rounded to the cent and limited to the tier's credit ceiling, and it refers to the excursion entry it compensates. The credit basis is the total of all amounts booked on that service, from its start up to the date of the credit, under the charge codes on the tier's credit basis list.

An excursion credit compensates the service charges only. Any loss in the value of the cargo is a matter for a cargo claim under the cargo claims terms, not for this credit.

## Qualification checklist

| Test | Earns a credit when |
|---|---|
| Duration | the excursion lasted at least the tier's qualifying minutes |
| Tier | its qualifying minutes figure is above zero |
| Cause | not the shipper's instruction, not an unsuitable set point, not cargo loaded warmer than the set point |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- Credit basis entries on a service: plug-in 180.00, remote monitoring 120.00 and special service 400.00, totalling 700.00. At an imagined rate of 40 percent the credit before limiting is 280.00; with an imagined ceiling of 250.00, the credit is 250.00.
- A basis of 333.33 at an imagined 25 percent gives 83.3325, which rounds to 83.33; with an imagined ceiling of 500.00 the credit stays at 83.33.
- With an imagined qualifying length of 120 minutes, an excursion of exactly 120 minutes qualifies, and one of 105 minutes does not.
- An excursion caused by the shipper's own instruction earns no credit, however long it lasted, although it is still entered on the record.
